issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) expect Stock.findStockIngredient(String) to exist, but the template defines Stock.findStockIngredient(String, boolean). Moreover, the template's add(...) and take(...) methods call findStockIngredient with a single String argument. This parameter mismatch causes a compile-time error and prevents students from implementing or using the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification and solution. Change or add an overload in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java to provide public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (which can delegate to the case-sensitive variant or use a default behavior). Alternatively, update the calls to findStockIngredient(...) to pass the boolean parameter consistently. Ensuring a single-parameter findStockIngredient(String) is present will align the template with the problem statement and solution and avoid compilation errors.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution define Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single parameter) but the template's Stock class provides findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (two parameters). This mismatch means students reading the specification and solution will look for a single-argument method and find a differently named/typed method in the starter code, causing confusion (and commented example code in Main expects the single-argument form).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock.findStockIngredient method to the single-argument signature (findStockIngredient(String name)) to match the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, provide an overloaded single-argument method that delegates to the two-argument variant with a sensible default (e.g., case-sensitive or case-insensitive) so examples and requirements map directly to the starter code.
